$comment: F6 live marker producers (services/event-core/live-markers.mjs), behind the feature flag 'live-markers' (off by default). The matching rules and thresholds are NOT here: they are read from data/clip/ranking.json (chat.intentPattern, chat.windowSec, chat.minMessages, chat.ratio, audio.floorLufs, audio.zThreshold, audio.minSpread, audio.minVoicedSec, peaks.minGapSec), so the live producers and the post-stream ranking (services/clip/clip_rank.py) use the same values. peaks.minGapSec is also the live dedupe window: at most one marker of each kind (chat intent, chat speed, audio) per that many seconds. This file holds only what exists live and not post-stream. status 'proposed' = agent defaults, not approved by the user and not tuned on a real stream (AGENTS.md: thresholds and windows are approved by the user, never invented).

chat.$comment: baselineSec: the running median of the rolling chat count uses at most this many past seconds (post-stream uses the whole recording). warmupSec: no chat-speed marker in the first this many seconds after the producer starts (chat starts from zero, so the opening burst would read as a spike every stream; 2026-11-06 stream-day mock run). warmupSec 120 chosen by the user 2026-11-06; the other values stay proposed.

audio.$comment: Live level = the highest libobs meter peak (dBFS, host mixer.list peakDb) over the counted sources, sampled every sampleMs, max per second. Post-stream uses short-term loudness (LUFS) of the recording; the same median/MAD z-score rule is applied to the live peak level (UNVERIFIED equivalence). sources: null = every active, unmuted source with a meter; or a list of mixer ids / project audio source ids. baselineSec: running median/MAD over at most this many past voiced seconds. hostTimeoutMs: one host call (marker.add, mixer.list) gives up after this.
